review_candidates.title: Software Engineer, Automotive and Industrial Architecture
review_candidates.description: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution. The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing. We are hiring multiple positions from early-career engineers to experienced architects focused on the different dimensions of dependable software: cybersecurity, quality, and safety. What does it take to bring the world’s open source software into mission-critical systems? At Canonical, we are driving the engineering discipline needed to build secure, reliable, and high-quality products that our automotive and industrial partners can depend on. Ubuntu is already the world’s most widely used Linux distribution in general; we want to make it the world’s best choice for the automotive and industrial sectors too. We operate at the boundary between upstream open source innovation and the industrial regulatory realities. Our engineers define the concepts, architectures, processes, verification strategies, and certification artifacts to transform a general-purpose platform into a dependable, certifiable foundation for automotive and industrial compute. This is systems-level engineering at scale, requiring precision, rigor, and a deep understanding of how complex software behaves in constrained, regulated environments. We are looking for engineers and architects who combine an open source hacker and builder mindset with respect for rigorous, standards-driven engineering. You will work across Canonical engineering teams and with leading industrial partners, helping to build this capability from the ground up and shaping how open source enters the most demanding technical domains. Location : This is a remote role based in the EMEA region. The role entails Translate automotive and industrial cybersecurity, quality and safety standards into actionable engineering requirements and perform gap analyses against current capabilities. Drive the creation of structured engineering artifacts, including requirements, traceability models, risk analysis, test strategies, and certification documentation. Collaborate with Canonical engineering teams to align development practices with industrial compliance needs. Design, implement, and execute verification and validation activities required to qualify Ubuntu and other components for regulated environments. Develop and improve automation and tooling to scale traceability, testing, compliance evidence generation, and reporting. Engage with industrial partners to understand their expectations, align external expectations and internal capabilities, and support audits and technical reviews. Contribute to the continuous improvement of Canonical’s internal processes and standards capability as the team scales. What We Are Looking For In You Strong software engineering foundation with experience in developing complex systems on Linux. Professional experience with C, C++, and Python in production environments. Demonstrated experience working within automotive, industrial, or other regulated environments governed by safety, cybersecurity, or quality standards (such as ISO 26262, ISO/SAE 21434, IEC 61508, IEC 62443, SOTIF, or (A)SPICE), and applying them in practice. Experience in system or software architecture, implementation, or verification and validation of complex embedded systems. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to produce precise technical documentation. Ability to collaborate effectively in a distributed team and engage with industrial partners. Additional Experience That Is Valuable Contributions to open source projects, particularly in the area of Software Defined Vehicles. Knowledge of Debian packaging. Experience with Rust or safety-critical software development. What We Offer Colleagues We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally. Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year Annual compensation review Recognition rewards Annual holiday leave Maternity and paternity leave Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues Priority Pass and travel upgrades for long-haul company events About Canonical Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since its inception in 2004. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical is an equal-opportunity employer We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity we will give your application fair consideration .

review_candidates.title: Funnel QA Specialist, DTC E-Commerce (Checkout & Tracking)
review_candidates.description: About HarZa Group HarZa Group builds and scales direct-to-consumer health and wellness brands. Our flagship brand is Rejuvacare, with RejuvaKnee as our hero product in chronic pain relief, and we are actively launching new brands across the portfolio. We run entirely on paid digital channels, ship primarily into the United States, and have grown twelve times in a single year with close to 150 people across more than 15 countries. We are remote-first by design and async-first by default. The Role Every funnel we publish carries paid traffic from the moment it goes live. When something breaks here, it does not break quietly in a staging environment. It breaks while we are spending money on it. The expensive failures in this business are rarely the obvious ones. A page that looks perfect but records the order under the wrong offer. An upsell that charges correctly and then sends the customer to a blank screen. A purchase event that fires twice and quietly corrupts the numbers the media buyer is optimizing against. A downsell path nobody walked, because everybody tested the version where the customer says yes. We are hiring a Funnel QA Specialist to be the person who walks those paths. You will test complete customer journeys rather than pages, inside Checkout Champ and across the funnels built on top of it. You will place test orders, follow every branch including the ones where the customer declines, verify that tracking fires correctly and only once, check the experience on mobile first because that is where our traffic is, and confirm that what went live matches what was approved. And you will do the part that matters more than any individual bug: when the same defect appears for the third time, you stop logging it as a new ticket and change the thing that keeps producing it. What You'll Do Test the full journey, not the page Walk complete funnels end to end before launch: advertorials, landing pages, VSL pages, quizzes, product pages, order forms, checkouts, upsells, downsells, declines and post-purchase flows Place test orders in Checkout Champ and validate pricing, offer configuration, order records, confirmation pages and what the customer actually receives Test the paths nobody volunteers to test: declined cards, abandoned flows, downsell branches, back-button behaviour, refreshes mid-checkout Test mobile first, then desktop, across the browsers our traffic actually uses Validate tracking as seriously as you validate checkout Confirm page view, add to cart, initiate checkout, purchase and custom events fire, fire once, and carry the correct values Use GTM preview, tag assistant and browser network inspection to verify rather than assume Flag tracking discrepancies early, because broken tracking corrupts decisions downstream before anyone notices the data is wrong Hold the line on quality Verify that live pages match approved copy, claims, pricing, imagery and brand standards Validate A/B test variations before launch, confirming both variants work and track cleanly Run regression checks on high-performing funnels whenever something is deployed near them Return work that has not been self-tested by the developer. Developer self-QA is a prerequisite here, and you are the second line of defence, not the first Make defects stop repeating Log defects with reproduction steps, severity, environment and evidence, clear enough that a developer can act without asking you a single question Verify fixes rather than assuming them Categorize recurring defects and their root causes, and push the change where it belongs: into the checklist, the template or the reusable component Build and maintain QC checklists for each page and funnel type, so quality becomes a property of the system rather than a property of your attention What Success Looks Like In your first 30 days, you know our funnels and offer structures, you are testing launches independently, and your defect reports are being acted on without follow-up questions. By day 90, we expect [X]% of launches going out with a complete journey check, escaped defects reduced to fewer than [X] per month, median time from defect reported to fix verified under [X], and the first set of standardized QC checklists live and in use. Beyond that, the measure is simple. The same defect should stop appearing, and the team should be able to ship faster because quality is built into the process rather than inspected at the end. Requirements What We're Looking For Hands-on QA experience testing live, customer-facing e-commerce or DTC flows. Not enterprise software QA, not QA of internal tools Practical experience with checkout flows, offers, upsells and post-purchase journeys. Checkout Champ is a strong plus; Shopify, ClickFunnels, Funnelish, Konnektive or a comparable funnel platform is expected Experience validating tracking and pixels with GTM, Meta Pixel, GA4 or similar Ability to read HTML and CSS and use browser developer tools to inspect elements, console errors and network requests Cross-browser and cross-device testing experience with mobile as the priority Risk-based judgment. You will often have forty minutes rather than four hours, and we need you to know what to check first and what can wait Precise written communication. A defect report you write should not generate a follow-up question The confidence to say something is not ready to launch, and the credibility to be believed when you say it Professional working English, written and spoken Reliable overlap with the 8am to 12pm EST collaboration window Experience building QC checklists or test plans is a plus. Automated testing experience is a plus, not a requirement How We Expect You to Work You are not a gate that says no. You are the reason we can ship fast without being reckless. We expect you to be direct about what is broken, specific about why, and constructive about what should change so it stops happening. We expect you to understand that a delayed launch has a cost and a broken launch has a different one, and to be able to tell us which one we are facing. We ship daily. Priorities move. Not every task arrives with complete context. The person who does well in this role asks the right question, makes a judgment call, and documents it. Benefits What We Offer A fully remote, async-first environment with a team across more than 15 countries. Paid time off, a wellness stipend, a company-funded computer allowance after a tenure milestone, a birthday gift card and an in-country meetup allowance. Real ownership of quality across a portfolio of fast-growing DTC brands. Our Values Own It. Make It Count. Find a Way. Master Your Craft. Win Together. These are operational standards here, used in hiring, performance and promotion decisions.

review_candidates.description: As a Software Developer at Schneider Electric, you will design and develop robust applications that meet user needs and enhance operational efficiency. You will work directly with customers to understand their requirements, then take ownership of the solution from end to end: architecture, design, implementation, testing, deployment, and handover. You will work as part of a global, cross-functional team, collaborating with colleagues around the world to build, enhance, and maintain high-quality software. You will implement application features alongside your teammates, take part in code reviews to maintain high-quality standards, and keep clear documentation of application design, functionality, and processes. As a technical specialist in application development, you will apply foundational knowledge of application engineering to deliver results, solve routine technical problems, and contribute to new technologies. You will work independently with general guidance, within defined parameters for quality, priorities, timing, and compliance. Your work will deliver reliable, efficient applications that streamline processes and improve productivity across the organization. Key Responsibilities Meet with customers and stakeholders to gather, analyze, and clarify business and technical requirements. Architect and design complete software solutions from A to Z, including the choice of programming languages, databases, frameworks, and cloud platforms. Design scalable, secure, and user-centric solutions on cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Implement application features based on requirements, working alongside team members to deliver high-quality, maintainable code. Conduct and participate in code reviews to uphold coding standards and quality. Test, deploy, and release solutions, ensuring reliability, performance, and data quality. Lead or support handover meetings, ensuring customers and support teams are fully equipped to use and maintain the delivered solution. Deliver sprint outputs on time, applying Agile methodologies to ensure iterative development and continuous value. Collaborate with cross-functional and globally distributed teams to resolve issues and deliver end-to-end solutions aligned with organizational priorities. Create and maintain documentation for application design, functionality, and processes. Act as a technical problem-solver, proposing optimizations and enhancements that improve efficiency and reduce manual effort. Follow company policies, procedures, quality standards, and compliance requirements. Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or Computer Engineering. Strong software engineering expertise, with the ability to design complete software solutions, including programming languages, databases, and system architecture. Hands-on knowledge of cloud platforms, including Microsoft Azure and AWS. Solid understanding of the software development lifecycle and how work flows in software companies, from requirements and design through development, testing, release, and support. Familiarity with Agile methodologies (Scrum, sprint planning, and iterative delivery). Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate business needs into logical technical solutions. Experience with version control, code reviews, and testing practices. Excellent communication, presentation, and customer-facing skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. Ability to work effectively in multicultural, international teams. Ability to manage time, meet sprint deadlines, and work independently with general guidance. Fluency in English is required. Motivated, eager to learn, and able to adapt quickly in a fast-paced environment. Why Join Us? At Schneider Electric, we are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where innovation thrives. Join us and help create reliable, innovative solutions that make a real impact across the organization. Rewards designed for you Our Total Rewards is our way of saying: We see you and we value you. It’s more than just pay and benefits—it’s a meaningful investment in you. It is designed to help you perform, grow, feel safe, and elevate your potential. We believe that our IMPACT values – Inclusion, Mastery, Purpose, Action, Curiosity, Teamwork – starts with us. IMPACT is also your invitation to join Schneider Electric where you can contribute to turning sustainability ambition into actions, no matter what role you play. It is a call to connect your career with the ambition of achieving a more resilient, efficient, and sustainable world. We are looking for IMPACT Makers; exceptional people who turn sustainability ambitions into actions at the intersection of automation, electrification, and digitization. We celebrate IMPACT Makers and believe everyone has the potential to be one. We look for a diverse team of individuals who possess different backgrounds, experiences, personalities and mindsets.
